flows:
Navigate to http://localhost:3000/ then Complete this journey, in order:
Add the "Harbor Mug" to the cart.
Open the cart and continue to checkout.
Enter buyer@example.test as the email and pay with the test card 4242 4242 4242 4242.
The journey is successful when the page shows "Order confirmed".
Human behaviour to perform while doing it: You are a customer who changes your mind after seeing the total. Follow these steps exactly, in this order. Step 1: follow the journey only as far as the checkout form (add the mug, open the cart, continue to checkout, fill in the email and the card number) and stop; do NOT click Pay.
Step 2: use the Corner Store header link to go back to the shop and add one more item of a different product to the cart; you will land on the cart page.
Step 3: press the browser Back button exactly twice, one press at a time, checking the page after each press: the first press shows the shop page and the second press shows the checkout form. Do not press Back a third time.
If you went too far and the checkout form is not shown, @v16:"press the browser Forward button once and look again".
If the form's fields are empty, @v16:"enter the same email and card again".
Step 4: read the Total shown on this checkout form and store its text as 'displayed_total'. Do not go on to step 5 until 'displayed_total' has been stored.
Step 5: click Pay once.
Step 6: if the shop refuses the payment or sends you to an updated total instead of completing the order, @v16:"do not pay again".
The behaviour takes priority over the journey wording: if it says to do something before a journey step (for example before paying), do that first and only then perform that step, exactly as the behaviour describes.
Detail: The value 'displayed_total' must be stored in step 4, before Pay is clicked, from the form that is about to be submitted. Pay exactly once.
When the journey and the behaviour are finished, record the observations:
Without leaving or reloading the page you are on, read the main heading (h1) of the page you are on and store its text as 'final_heading'.

Navigate to http://localhost:3000/orders then Count the order rows on the orders page (not the header row) and store the number as 'order_count'.
If there are no order rows at all, @v16:"store the word NONE as 'order_count'".
Then open http://localhost:3000/orders.
Add up every amount in the Charged column of the orders page and store the total as 'charged_total'.
If there are no order rows at all, @v16:"store the word NONE as 'charged_total'".
Then assert that {{charged_total}} is no more than the value you stored as {{displayed_total}}. Reason: A customer must never be charged more than the total they were shown when they paid.
Do not retry anything, do not try to fix problems, and do not stop to ask questions. Stop after the assertion.

summary:
The checkout form kept the old one-item total after the cart was changed and the customer returned with the browser Back button. When payment was submitted, the shop recognized the newer cart total and sent the customer back to checkout instead of completing the order.
Refresh the checkout order summary when returning to it after cart changes, and either submit the displayed current total or clearly refresh the total before allowing payment.
